issues.t: Connecting rod bearings can fail and ruin the engine (recall)
issues.sym: Knocking from the engine, a check engine or oil pressure warning, loss of power, or the engine stalling.
issues.why: Some 2.0L turbo engines were built with damaged or contaminated connecting rod bearings, which can wear quickly and cause engine failure. Covered by NHTSA campaigns 22V-753 (2022-2023) and 23V-593 (2024).
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls right away. The dealer inspects the engine and replaces it if needed, free of charge. Stop driving if you hear knocking.

issues.t: Engine shuts off while driving or at stops
issues.sym: The engine cuts out when slowing, at a stop sign or in traffic, sometimes with a start/stop message, and must be restarted by hand. Steering gets heavy when it happens.
issues.why: Owners report many stalls on these years. Dealers have pointed to the evaporative (EVAP) purge valve and charcoal canister, fuel injectors and start/stop faults, and some cars stalled even with auto start/stop turned off.
issues.next: Note when it happens and any warning messages, and take it to a dealer while under warranty. Ask about open recalls and software updates; the fuel injector recall can also cause stalling.

issues.t: Door wiring corrosion can delay side airbags (recall)
issues.sym: Often no warning, but some owners see the airbag light, windows going down on their own, or the parking brake applying itself.
issues.why: Contacts in the front door wiring connectors can corrode, which can delay the front side airbag in a side crash. VW recalled these vehicles under NHTSA campaign 22V-152.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer secures or replaces the harness free of charge.

issues.t: Windows open and parking brake applies on their own
issues.sym: Windows roll down by themselves, the electronic parking brake grabs at low speed or while in gear, and the car thinks the driver door is open.
issues.why: Dealers have traced many cases to a faulty driver door switch or corroded door wiring harness, the same area covered by the door wiring recall.
issues.next: Do not ignore it: a parking brake that applies at speed is dangerous. Have a dealer check the driver door harness and switch, and make sure the door wiring recall is done.

issues.t: Passenger airbag can switch off with an adult in the seat (recall)
issues.sym: The PASSENGER AIRBAG OFF light comes on while an adult is sitting in the front seat.
issues.why: A wiring fault in the front passenger occupant detection system can switch off the passenger airbag. Covered by NHTSA campaigns 23V-215 (2020) and 24V-464 (2020-2024).
issues.next: Keep adults out of the front seat if the light is wrong, and check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer replaces the sensor mat and harness free of charge.

issues.t: Sudden braking from the Front Assist system
issues.sym: The car brakes hard on its own with nothing in the way, or the Front Assist warning comes on for no reason.
issues.why: Owners report the automatic emergency braking (Front Assist) and lane assist reacting to things that are not there. A class action was filed over sudden braking on 2020-2023 models.
issues.next: Keep the front sensor and windshield camera area clean, ask the dealer about software updates, and report each event to NHTSA. You can turn Front Assist off temporarily in the settings menu.

issues.t: Brake squeal, grinding and early pad wear
issues.sym: Squealing or grinding brakes, and pads or rotors that need replacing well before 30,000 miles.
issues.why: Owners report noisy brakes and short pad and rotor life on these years. Dealers have blamed rust buildup on the rotors in some cases.
issues.next: Have the pads and rotors measured. Quality pads and resurfaced or new rotors usually fix the noise; if it starts under warranty, report it to the dealer.

issues.t: Touchscreen freezes, reboots or goes blank
issues.sym: The center screen freezes, restarts or goes black, taking radio, climate controls and the backup camera with it; some drivers see warnings that safety systems are disabled.
issues.why: Owners report repeated infotainment failures. On some 2021-2022 vehicles a faulty memory chip in the infotainment unit is a known cause.
issues.next: Try a full restart and ask the dealer for software updates and any open recalls. If the screen stays dead, the unit is replaced under warranty.

issues.t: Backup camera can go black from an infotainment fault (recall)
issues.sym: No backup camera picture when you shift into reverse.
issues.why: A defective memory chip in the infotainment unit can stop the rear camera image from showing. VW recalled these vehicles under NHTSA campaign 22V-514.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer repairs or replaces the unit for free.

issues.t: Backup camera image can be delayed, distorted or missing (recall)
issues.sym: The rear camera picture shows up late, looks distorted, or does not appear at all when reversing.
issues.why: Software errors in the camera system can delay, distort or blank the image, especially after a low-voltage event. Covered by NHTSA campaigns 24V-480, 25V-334 and 26V-473.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer updates the software free of charge.

issues.t: Fuel injectors may leak fuel (recall)
issues.sym: A fuel smell, hard starting or stalling.
issues.why: Some fuel injectors were assembled without their filter, so debris can get in and the injector can leak fuel, a fire risk. VW recalled these vehicles under NHTSA campaign 22V-245.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer replaces the injectors free of charge.

issues.t: Blocked A/C drain can leak onto the airbag module (recall)
issues.sym: Wet front passenger carpet or water under the center console.
issues.why: A blocked A/C drain tube can let water reach the airbag control module, which could set off the airbags. VW recalled these vehicles under NHTSA campaign 21V-892.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the drain and module checked for free.

issues.t: Front steering knuckles can crack (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from the front suspension, pulling, or loose-feeling steering.
issues.why: Some front steering knuckles were damaged in production or can crack at the strut mount. VW recalled these vehicles under NHTSA campaigns 20V-712 and 21V-026.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. Some owners were told not to drive until inspected; the dealer replaces the knuckles for free.

issues.t: Factory Continental tires can fail at the sidewall (recall)
issues.sym: A bulge in the tire sidewall or sudden air loss.
issues.why: Some 20-inch Continental CrossContact LX Sport tires may have been over-cured and can fail. Covered by NHTSA campaign 20V-702.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. Affected tires are replaced free of charge.

issues.t: Front seat frame welds may be weak (recall)
issues.sym: Nothing you will notice in normal driving.
issues.why: The front seat frame and backrest adjuster may not have been welded correctly and could break in a rear crash. Covered by NHTSA campaign 20V-505.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the seat inspected and repaired for free.

issues.t: Tire pressure warning may miss low tires (recall)
issues.sym: The tire pressure light may not come on if all four tires lose air slowly together.
issues.why: The tire pressure monitoring software may not detect an equal pressure loss in all tires. Covered by NHTSA campaign 22V-815.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls; the dealer updates the software for free. Check tire pressures yourself monthly.

issues.t: Rear trailing arm bolts can loosen (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk or knock from the left rear, or the vehicle pulling.
issues.why: The driver-side rear trailing arm bolts may loosen and fall out, which could let the arm break and cause loss of control. Covered by NHTSA campaign 22V-807.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer replaces the bolts free of charge.

issues.t: Trailer hitch bolts may be loose (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from the hitch when towing.
issues.why: Trailer hitch mounting bolts may not have been tightened enough. Covered by NHTSA campaign 22V-657.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and do not tow until it is fixed. The dealer tightens or replaces the bolts for free.

issues.t: Brake lines can leak at the fittings (recall)
issues.sym: Brake fluid drips near the wheels, a low brake fluid warning, or a soft pedal.
issues.why: Brake lines may leak at their threaded connections, which can lengthen stopping distances. Covered by NHTSA campaign 22V-718.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. If the pedal feels soft, do not drive; have it towed to a dealer.

issues.t: Chassis and brake bolts may be loose (recall)
issues.sym: Clunks or rattles from the suspension, or a change in handling or braking.
issues.why: Some chassis, brake or suspension bolts may not have been tightened at the factory. Covered by NHTSA campaign 25V-434.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer replaces the bolts free of charge.

issues.t: Brake master cylinder may have the wrong part (recall)
issues.sym: A brake pedal that sinks or brakes that feel weak.
issues.why: A wrong spring retainer in the brake master cylinder can block the fluid port and cause a loss of braking. Covered by NHTSA campaign 24V-723.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer replaces the master cylinder for free.

issues.t: Engine cover can come loose and melt after service (recall)
issues.sym: A burning plastic smell from the engine bay after an oil change or other service.
issues.why: The engine cover may be put back wrong after service and touch hot engine parts, a fire risk. Covered by NHTSA campaign 25V-100.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer removes the cover free of charge.

issues.t: Transmission may lose drive suddenly (recall)
issues.sym: The vehicle suddenly loses power to the wheels while driving.
issues.why: A small number of transmissions were built incorrectly. Covered by NHTSA campaign 25V-081.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer replaces the transmission free of charge.

issues.t: LED daytime running light failure
issues.sym: One daytime running light or headlight section goes dark with no warning.
issues.why: Owners report the LED running lights failing, and because the LEDs are built in, the whole headlight assembly is replaced. Parts have been on back order.
issues.next: Check whether the car is still under warranty, since a headlight assembly is expensive.

issues.t: Tire choppy wear and road noise
issues.sym: Increasing road noise and tires wearing in uneven, choppy patches at low mileage.
issues.why: Owners report early tire chop on this year; alignment and tire rotation intervals play a big part.
issues.next: Have the alignment checked and rotate the tires every 5,000-7,500 miles.
